clue.text: Radical diet saving me when ailing

indicators.note: something ailing is out of sorts, so the letters of the two words before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sick is told an extreme regime of eating will rescue them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ailing' is the anagram signal on SAVING ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Shunning all animal products is a far-reaching, uncompromising eating regime, hence a radical diet.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeker by choice, put out over conservation body

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes over, taking the place of, the conservation body

parts.note: voluntary means done by choice
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity
put knocked out of shape gives its letters jumbled, P T U

explanation.surface: A hedonist willingly ejected from a charity that looks after old houses.
explanation.walkthrough: NT in VOLUNTARY is replaced by PTU, PUT scrambled since 'out' means awry; 'over' signals the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to luxury and sensual gratification is a hedonist, a seeker of pleasure.

clue.text: Siege once broken, involving cold study of rock structures?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the abbreviation for cold
broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A historical siege breaking down, with cold weather involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' gives GEOSIENCE from SIEGE ONCE, and C goes in after GEOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth science covers geology, the study of rocks and their structures, among other fields; hence the query.

clue.text: Preceding answer half upset relative

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
only the latter five of the ten letters are used

parts.note: the preceding answer is the solution to 2 down, the clue before this one

explanation.surface: Someone from the family is half annoyed at the last response.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of the previous answer is IENCE, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Disarming description of solo performance?

parts.note: doing something alone without help is literally doing it with only one of your two hands, a description that removes an arm, so to speak

explanation.surface: A charming way of describing a one-person show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disarming' seems to mean charming, but read literally it means losing an arm, leaving just one hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting entirely alone, without assistance, is the idiomatic sense of having only one hand at work.

clue.text: Hunting dog to risk going round equine

indicators.note: the word for risking wraps itself around the animal, enclosing it

parts.note: to risk money is to bet it
an ass is an equine animal, a donkey

explanation.surface: A gamble on a hound that goes round with a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged hound bred for tracking hares and rabbits by scent.

clue.text: Prime locks, securing foremost of Chippendale furniture

indicators.note: the two words hold the first letter tight between them

parts.note: to prime a weapon is to arm it
locks of hair are hairs

indicators.note: the first letter of the cabinet-maker's name is taken

explanation.surface: Fine curls holding together a piece of Chippendale furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Padded seats with side rests are items of furniture; the plural noun matches the collective sense.

clue.text: TV show to begin with loss of ship in radio message

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: a radio message is heard rather than seen, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a wreck is the loss of a ship at sea

explanation.surface: A broadcast opening with news by radio of a sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running science-fiction series about the starship Enterprise is a television programme.

clue.text: See 7
Facilities observed by day — an unsettled issue

parts.note: the facilities is a euphemism for the toilet, the loo
observed means seen

explanation.surface: Toilets inspected by daylight leave a problem still unresolved.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter left untied or unfinished is an idiomatic stray thread still to be dealt with.

clue.text: Transfix the French, after millions invested in beer

indicators.note: the French article comes after the beer piece in the answer
the letter for millions is put inside the beer, as money is put into something

parts.note: IPA is India pale ale, a beer
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
le is the French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A sentence about money sunk into French beer, pinning someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix is to pierce right through, as with a spike or stake.

clue.text: Abandoned magazine — junior editor's copy framed by nude dancing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the middle pieces like a picture frame
dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, is a junior editor; the 's adds S
to crib is to copy; a crib is a copied answer

explanation.surface: A publication dropped after an editor's copy shows a naked dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles the nude letters, which 'framed by' splits to sit either side; the definition reads as a verb phrase, gave up a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancelling a regular subscription means having given up a periodical, so the past verb fits.

clue.text: Meal? Wanted, first to last, to participate in bash

indicators.note: the altered word joins in, going inside the word for a blow

parts.note: a bash is a blow, a punch

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for wanted is moved to its end

parts.note: wanted means lacked

explanation.surface: Someone hungry wants food before joining a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the opening L to the end of the word for wanted; 'to participate in' puts the result after the P of the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwiches and the like boxed up to eat away from home are an example of a meal, hence the query.

clue.text: Straight line maker limiting one more inclined to spread out

indicators.note: the outer word bounds the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: a stretcher is a brick or stone laid lengthwise, making a straight line along a wall
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ruler restricting one individual who likes to sprawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a greater tendency to extend or lengthen out is comparatively more elastic.

clue.text: Fish satisfied, rising around river for part of the year?

parts.note: a school is a group of fish swimming together

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the river letter
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to have met a demand is to have satisfied it

explanation.surface: A happy angler going up a river at some point in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MET into TEM, and R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the teaching periods into which the academic calendar is divided, hence the query.

clue.text: Finish off American power with invasion by group of nations

indicators.note: the bloc of nations invades, getting inside the other letters

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
the EU is the European Union, a group of nations

explanation.surface: Wiping out American power as a bloc of nations invades.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust something completely is to consume it until nothing remains.

clue.text: Fell in, and put to work in large numbers

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new order, shaped into another word

explanation.surface: Someone joined the ranks and was given lots of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing in abundance means there are lots of something; the adjective works in sentences either way.

clue.text: Exploratory process Curie deployed with this

indicators.note: deployed means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Marie Curie putting a method into use in her research.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule-of-thumb method of discovery by trial and error is an exploratory approach to a problem.

clue.text: Denies accommodating some of the army cowards

indicators.note: the word for denies houses the army unit within it

parts.note: to recant is to deny or retract what one said
RE is the Royal Engineers, part of the British army

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take in deserters from the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an old word for a craven or faithless person, so the plural means cowards.

clue.text: Sort out old river, taking new direction

indicators.note: the letters head off a different way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: An ancient river changes course, perhaps needing someone to fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to or deal with a problem is to fix it.

clue.text: Speculative article? Old article revamped

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: revamped means remade, so the letters of the second article are reworked

explanation.surface: A conjectural piece of writing that is an old one rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculative means based on conjecture rather than practice, the same as abstract or hypothetical.

clue.text: Temperature roughly observed in part of body

parts.note: or so means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: A rough temperature reading taken on part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed in' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human frame, without the head or limbs, is a part of the body.

clue.text: TV show with daughter and son gaining power in time

indicators.note: the family members and power are placed inside the word for time

parts.note: a day is a period of time

indicators.note: the son gains the power, which joins on after him

parts.note: an arm can stand for power or might, as in the arm of the law

explanation.surface: A family viewing: a girl and boy getting stronger over time.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic BBC sitcom about the Home Guard in the Second World War is a television programme.

clue.text: See 22
Aimless dispute in marketing industry?

parts.note: AD stands for advertising, the marketing industry
a rift is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A quarrel among advertisers leaves the business directionless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, a rift in advertising is simply AD followed by RIFT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting without purpose or direction is the figurative sense of floating loose.

clue.text: Vain American, dull person, set to detain one inside

indicators.note: the set holding one goes inside the dull person

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person

indicators.note: the set holds the one within it, as a captor detains someone

parts.note: a TV is a television set
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A conceited, tedious American plans to keep someone captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a television set; 'to detain' and 'inside' nest one container in another, with the dull person outermost.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt made in vain is fruitless, coming to nothing.

clue.text: Mythical monster — namely, the reverse of a friend

parts.note: sc, short for Latin scilicet, means namely

indicators.note: the word for a friend is turned round, written backwards

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A monster described as the opposite of a companion: an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey this six-headed sea beast faced Charybdis across a narrow strait.

clue.text: I follow sheep round middle of field in symbolic representation

indicators.note: the word for follow goes round the central letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word field is taken

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheepdog-like scene: I trail a sheep around the middle of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I follow' looks like I coming after something, but follow is DOG beside I.
explanation.definitionFit: A written character standing for an idea rather than a sound is a symbol representing something.
